cues.zh: 后来准备演讲时，这让我想到几十年前我们两个社会之间发生的一些事。
cues.en: Then when it came to giving a talk, it's uh made me think about some things that transpired between both of our both of our societies, uh some decades ago.

cues.zh: 比如1957年，苏联发射了Sputnik，这是世界上第一颗成功绕地球运行的人造卫星。
cues.en: For example, in 1957, uh when the Soviet Union launched Sputnik, uh the world's first man-made satellite that orbited the Earth successfully.

cues.zh: 而在美国，大家都慌了，他们不喜欢在太空领域落后，说：天哪，我们得追上去。我们必须在90天内把一颗卫星送入轨道。
cues.en: Uh back in the USA, everybody freaked out about this, uh they didn't like being behind in space and said, oh my god, uh we got to catch up. We have to get a satellite into orbit in 90 days.

cues.zh: 这听起来简直疯了。
cues.en: Which seems crazy.

cues.zh: 确实如此，我们的第一次尝试在发射台上爆炸了。
cues.en: And it was, uh our first attempt blew up on the launch pad.

cues.zh: 但第二次尝试成功了，那是1958年1月31日。
cues.en: Uh, but the second attempt succeeded, that was January 31st, 1958.

cues.zh: 距离最初那次发射差不多120天。
cues.en: It was almost 120 days after that initial launch.

cues.zh: 按现代标准看，这相当快。
cues.en: It's pretty fast by modern standards.

cues.zh: 然后在1961年4月，Yuri Gagarin 成为第一个绕地球轨道飞行的人，呃，这又成了全世界的头条新闻。
cues.en: Then in April 1961, Yuri Gagarin became the first human being to orbit the Earth and again, uh that made news all over the world.

cues.zh: 大家都对此印象深刻。
cues.en: Everybody was very impressed by that.

cues.zh: 而在美国，呃，人们很不满。
cues.en: And back in the United States, uh people were upset.

cues.zh: 因为，我们又一次落后了；而我们在落后的，显然正是太空竞赛。
cues.en: Because again, we were behind, we were behind in what was becoming clear was the space race.

cues.zh: 我们不喜欢这样，那我们要怎么应对？
cues.en: And we didn't like that and what were we going to do about it?

cues.zh: 所以，呃，1961年5月，在那次飞行一个月后，呃，我们当时的总统 Kennedy 向国会发表演讲，说：听着，如果我们要追赶、不想永远落后，就得干一件大事。
cues.en: So, um in may 1961, one month after that flight, uh our president at the time, Kennedy, made a speech to Congress saying like, look, if we're going to catch up and not be behind forever, we have to do something big.

cues.zh: 我们必须投入大量资金、大量资源，我们要去月球，对吧？
cues.en: We have to commit a lot of money, a lot of resources, we're going to go to the moon, right?

cues.zh: 那算是个疯狂的想法；1962年，他在一次著名的公开演讲中重申了这一点。
cues.en: And that was kind of a crazy idea and in 1962, he reiterated this in a famous public speech.

cues.zh: 他说，听着，我们要在十年结束前登上月球。
cues.en: And he said, look, we're going to go to the moon before the decade is over.

cues.zh: 这太疯狂了。
cues.en: And that was crazy.

cues.zh: 这真的很疯狂，因为我们之前根本没做过任何类似的事。
cues.en: It was really crazy because we hadn't done anything remotely like that.

cues.zh: 但你瞧，最终我们还真做到了。
cues.en: Um, but low and behold, uh eventually we did.

cues.zh: 于是，阿波罗11号于1969年7月16日发射，赶在这个十年结束之前。
cues.en: So, Apollo 11 launched on July 16th, 1969, um before the decade was over.

cues.zh: 就在今年，出了一部非常好的纪录片，讲的就是整个任务。
cues.en: And just this year, uh there's a very good documentary that came out about this whole mission.

cues.zh: 它完全由NASA在任务期间拍摄的原始影像构成，这些影像一直被搁在柜子和壁橱里。
cues.en: Um what it is is it's made of all original footage that NASA NASA took during the mission that's been sitting away in cupboards and closets.

cues.zh: 他们修复了这些影像，并大致重现了亲历这次任务的感觉。
cues.en: And they restored the footage and they sort of made a recreation of what it was like to live through this mission.

cues.zh: 我要放一段这部纪录片的短片，让你们感受一下整件事的规模有多大。
cues.en: And I'm going to play a short excerpt uh from that documentary just to give you uh a sense of what the scale of this whole thing was like.

cues.zh: 这内容真不少。
cues.en: It's a lot.

cues.zh: 而且很疯狂。我们在大约 12 年里，从一无所有做到了那一切。
cues.en: And it's crazy. We we went from nothing to all that stuff in something like 12 years.

cues.zh: 在 Sputnik 上天之前，美国没什么航天计划，而到最后，我们有了那么多东西。
cues.en: Before Sputnik flew, we didn't have much of a space program in the United States and in the end, we had all that stuff.

cues.zh: 当然，之后我们继续搞太空项目，对吧？
cues.en: And then of course, after that, we continued to do space things, right?

cues.zh: 我们造了这架航天飞机。
cues.en: We made this space shuttle.

cues.zh: 它看起来真的很酷。
cues.en: It seemed like a really cool thing.

cues.zh: 就像科幻小说里的飞船，能起飞，还能再降落。
cues.en: It's like a ship out of science fiction. It could like take off and then land again.

cues.zh: 太棒了，对吧？
cues.en: That's so great, right?

cues.zh: 问题是，其实它大部分部件都回不来，比如背景里那些储箱，所以飞行成本非常高。
cues.en: Problem is, actually most of it couldn't land, like those tanks in the background there, and therefore, it was very expensive to fly.

cues.zh: 而且它非常不可靠。
cues.en: Uh and it was very unreliable.

cues.zh: 有几次任务中有人丧生，出于这些原因，我们决定不再使用它。
cues.en: People died on this on a couple of different missions and we decided to stop using it for all of these reasons.

cues.zh: 所以在那之后，如果我们想把人类送入轨道，
cues.en: So after that, if we wanted to put people in orbit,

cues.zh: 就得搭联盟号上去。
cues.en: We had to get a ride on the Soyuz.

cues.zh: 呃，从那以后，我们航天计划的轨迹就一路向下。
cues.en: Uh and then from there, the trajectory of our space program kept going downwards.

cues.zh: 呃，所以如果你在2002或2005年前后跟像我这样的人聊聊，
cues.en: Uh and so if you talk to somebody like me sometime around the year 2002 or 2005,

cues.zh: 我们都有这种态度：这不是很可惜吗？
cues.en: We all had this attitude like, isn't it a shame?

cues.zh: 就像美国以前在太空里做过那么多酷炫的事，而现在我们好像什么都不做了。
cues.en: Like the USA used to do all this cool stuff in space, and now we like don't really do anything.

cues.zh: 我们设想的科幻未来并不会真的发生，而且我们也不觉得它会改变。
cues.en: And the science fiction future that we visualized isn't really going to happen, and we don't ever see that changing.

cues.zh: 但你能怎么办呢？唉，耸耸肩，对吧？
cues.en: And but what can you do about it? Oh well, shrug, right?

cues.zh: 这就是所有人的态度。
cues.en: That was just everybody's attitude.

cues.zh: 呃，但也不完全是所有人，对吧？
cues.en: Uh but not quite everybody, right?

cues.zh: 后来某一天，有个人靠一个网站赚了一大笔钱，然后说：嘿，呃，我想为此做点什么。
cues.en: At some point, somebody came along who made a bunch of uh money on a website and said, hey, um I want to do something about this.

cues.zh: 尽管没有火箭经验，我还是要创办一家公司来发射火箭，做比以往更大的事。
cues.en: Despite having no rocket experience, I'm going to start a company to launch rockets and to do bigger stuff than we've ever done before.

cues.zh: 所以这里有一段视频节选，讲他为什么做这些事。
cues.en: And so here's an excerpt of a video about why he did that stuff.

cues.zh: 嗯，然后是成为多行星物种，以及让文明走向太空。
cues.en: Um, then there's becoming a multi-planet species and space for civilization.

cues.zh: 这不是必然的。
cues.en: This is not inevitable.

cues.zh: 很重要的一点是要认识到：这不是必然的。
cues.en: It's very important to appreciate. This is not inevitable.

cues.zh: 可持续能源的未来，我认为在很大程度上是必然的。
cues.en: The sustainable energy future, I think is largely inevitable.

cues.zh: 呃，但成为太空文明绝对不是必然的。
cues.en: Uh but being space civilization is definitely not inevitable.

cues.zh: 如果看看太空领域的进展，1969 年我们能把 72 送上月球。
cues.en: If you look at the at the the progress in space, in 1969, we were able to send 72 to the moon.

cues.zh: 嗯，然后我们有了航天飞机。
cues.en: Um, then we had the the space shuttle.

cues.zh: 航天飞机只能把人送到近地轨道。
cues.en: The the space shuttle could only take people to low Earth orbit.

cues.zh: 后来航天飞机退役了，美国无法再把任何人送入轨道。
cues.en: Then the space shuttle retired and the United States could take no one to orbit.

cues.zh: 所以这就是趋势。趋势就是一路降到零。
cues.en: So that's the trend. A trend is like down to nothing.

cues.zh: 这并不是说，人们认为技术会自动进步时，我就错了。
cues.en: This is not I am mistaken when when they think that technology just automatically improves.

cues.zh: 技术并不会自动进步。
cues.en: It does not automatically improve.

cues.zh: 只有很多人拼命努力把它做得更好，它才会进步。
cues.en: It it only improves if a lot of people work very hard to make it better.

cues.zh: 而且实际上，我觉得它自己本身是会退化的。
cues.en: And actually, it it will, I think, by itself, degrade, actually.

cues.zh: 看看古埃及这样的伟大文明，他们能建造金字塔。
cues.en: You look at great civilizations like Ancient Egypt and they were able to make the pyramids.

cues.zh: 后来他们忘了怎么建。
cues.en: And they forgot how to do that.

cues.zh: 还有罗马人，他们建造了那些令人惊叹的高架渠。
cues.en: Um and the Romans, they built these incredible aqueducts.

cues.zh: 他们忘了怎么建。
cues.en: They forgot how to do it.

cues.zh: 所以他的想法相当成功。
cues.en: So his idea was pretty successful.

cues.zh: 呃，而今天，我们已经能让火箭着陆，还在认真讨论最早2024年再执行一次登月任务。
cues.en: Uh and today, we're like landing rockets and we're seriously talking about doing another moon mission as soon as the year 2024.

cues.zh: 看看那会不会真的发生吧，呃，但我们确实在认真讨论这件事；考虑到不久前我们还在什么水平，这已经挺不错了。
cues.en: We'll see if that actually happens, uh but really talking about it seriously and that's a pretty good thing given where we were not long ago.

cues.zh: 嗯，Elon 提到了过去一些曾经很了不起、后来却失传的成就，我想再讲几个这样的例子。
cues.en: Um, so Elon talked about a few things from the past that were great achievements that have been lost and I wanted to go through a few more of those.

cues.zh: 再强调一下他的观点：技术会自动退化。
cues.en: To reiterate his point that technology automatically degrades.

cues.zh: 嗯，你看到的这个东西是 Lycurgus Cup。
cues.en: Uh this thing here that you see is the Lycurgus Cup.

cues.zh: 嗯，这是一件文物，被发现后确定可追溯到公元 300 年的罗马帝国时期。
cues.en: Uh this was a relic uh found uh and dated back to the Roman Empire, 300 AD.

cues.zh: 它是玻璃做的，而制它的这种玻璃是已知世界上最早的纳米材料，对吧？
cues.en: And it's made of glass, and this glass that it's made of is the world's earliest known nanomaterial, okay?

cues.zh: 玻璃的颜色会随观察方式变化，比如光源在什么位置。
cues.en: The color of the glass changes based on how you look at it, like where the light source is.

cues.zh: 所以，如果你站在玻璃前面看它，而光源大概就在你这边，也就是说你看到的是反射光，
cues.en: So if you're looking at it standing in front of the glass, and the light source is sort of over here with you, so that you're seeing it with reflected light,

cues.zh: 那么高脚杯就是绿色的。
cues.en: then the goblet is green.

cues.zh: 但如果光穿过它，呃，酒杯就是红色的。
cues.en: But if light is passing through it, uh the goblet is red.

cues.zh: 公元300年他们就有这个了，对吧？
cues.en: They had this in 300 AD, right?

cues.zh: 后来罗马帝国灭亡，那项知识就失传了，呃，基本等于永远失传。
cues.en: And then the Roman Empire fell and that knowledge was lost uh until basically forever.

cues.zh: 呃，它的原理其实，你知道，直到1990年左右才被弄明白。
cues.en: Um the way this worked was actually, you know, it got figured out around 1990.

cues.zh: 呃，玻璃里布满极小的银颗粒和金颗粒，非常小，我是说50到70纳米，小到用普通显微镜根本看不见。
cues.en: Um the glass is suffused with very small particles of silver and gold by very small, I mean 50 to 70 nanometers, which is so small you would not be able to see them with a physical microscope.

cues.zh: 得用电子显微镜才能看到这些颗粒，对吧？
cues.en: You would require an electron microscope to see these particles, right?

cues.zh: 但后来某个时候罗马帝国灭亡了，他们忘了怎么做。
cues.en: But at some point the Roman Empire fell and they forgot how to do it.

cues.zh: 呃，这里面倾注了大量工艺。你看，小人物身体所在的位置在内侧被掏空，是为了让他更偏紫色光泽，而背景偏红。
cues.en: Um, a lot of craftsmanship went into this. Uh you could see, you know, how it's hollowed out on the inside where the little guy's body is to give him more of a purple sheen as opposed to a red in the background.

cues.zh: 如果你今天听到人们谈论这个，或者自己去查资料，他们往往对它持一种不屑的态度。
cues.en: And if you hear people talk about this today or you or you read up on this, um they tend to have a dismissive attitude toward it.

cues.zh: 比如，哦，愚蠢的罗马人不懂技术，他们可能根本不知道是银和金造成了这个效果。
cues.en: Like, oh, the stupid Romans didn't understand technology, they probably didn't even know it was silver and gold that made this happen.

cues.zh: 嗯，这大概只是个意外，他们只做出了五个这样的东西，对吧？
cues.en: Uh it was probably just an accident and they made like five of these, right?

cues.zh: 这完全是无稽之谈。
cues.en: Which is complete nonsense.

cues.zh: 任何真正动手做东西、而不是只写文章的人都知道，没有持续迭代和改进的过程，你不可能得到这么好的结果。
cues.en: Like, anybody who actually builds things, as opposed to just writing about them, knows, you do not get a result this good without a constant process of iteration and refinement.

cues.zh: 你可以想象，最初可能有个意外，比如有人想让玻璃闪闪发光，试着往里面加了银和金，然后注意到了一点点变色。
cues.en: You can imagine there would be some initial accident, like maybe somebody wanted to make glass sparkly and they tried to put silver and gold in it, and then they noticed a little bit of discoloration.

cues.zh: 他们会问，为什么那儿会有这个？
cues.en: And they said like, why is that there?

cues.zh: 也许他们会追问，如果我改变配比会怎样，对吧？
cues.en: And maybe they pursued that like, what happens when I change the proportions, right?

cues.zh: 比如玻璃该有多厚？
cues.en: What how thick should the glass be?

cues.zh: 像这么好的工程成果，需要很长时间。
cues.en: Like engineering results this good takes a long time.

cues.zh: 这意味着，在罗马，人们在做一些我们今天会认为是材料科学的事情。
cues.en: And what that means is that in Rome, people were doing something that we would recognize today as material science.

cues.zh: 后来这些失传了。
cues.en: And then that was lost.

cues.zh: 还发生了别的事。
cues.en: Other stuff happened.

cues.zh: 比如在拜占庭帝国，他们有火焰喷射器，可不是小打小闹的那种。
cues.en: Like in the Byzantine Empire, they had flamethrowers and not like little dinky things.

cues.zh: 他们在船腹中装有巨大的压力容器，通过金属管喷射出一种类似凝固汽油的物质，用来烧毁附近的船只。
cues.en: They had giant pressurized vessels in the bellies of ships that shot out a napalm like substance out of metal tubes that they would use to incinerate neighboring vessels.

cues.zh: 嗯，说它像凝固汽油，是因为水浇不灭这种火，对吧？
cues.en: Um, it was napalm like in the sense that like water would not put this fire out, right?

cues.zh: 这是一种非常厉害的武器。它是拜占庭帝国的国家机密。
cues.en: It was very serious weapon. It was a state secret of the Byzantine Empire.

cues.zh: 几百年来，他们一次次用它保卫君士坦丁堡，
cues.en: They used it to defend Constantinople over and over again for hundreds of years,

cues.zh: 直到有一天，不知什么原因，他们再也做不到这一点了，这项军事机密也就逐渐失传了。
cues.en: until one day they couldn't really do that anymore for whatever reason, and this military secret just faded from knowledge.

cues.zh: 现在没人知道怎么做了，对吧？
cues.en: Nobody knows how to do it now, right?

cues.zh: 显然我们重新发明了火焰喷射器，但它们不一样。
cues.en: Obviously we've reinvented flamethrowers, but they're different.

cues.zh: 嗯，这是安提基特拉机械，呃，名字来自希腊的一座岛，它就是在那里的一艘沉船上被发现的。
cues.en: Um, this is the Antikythera mechanism, uh which is named after an island in uh Greece where this was found on a sunken ship.

cues.zh: 它只是一块锈蚀的金属疙瘩，或者好几块锈蚀的金属疙瘩。
cues.en: It was just a corroded hunk of metal or a number of corroded hunks of metal.

cues.zh: 但很明显，呃，它们最初被发现时，就看出里面有齿轮，后来人们也对此做了分析。
cues.en: But it was very clear, uh when they were originally discovered that gears were involved and over time people analyzed this.

cues.zh: 他们发现这是一部机械日历，能用来回答比如现在是哪一年？
cues.en: They realized it's a mechanical calendar that was used to say things like, you know, what what year is it?

cues.zh: 月相是什么？行星现在会在什么位置？
cues.en: What are the phases of the moon? Where are the planets going to be right now?

cues.zh: 下一届奥运会在什么时候，对吧？
cues.en: When is the next Olympic Games, right?

cues.zh: 人们扫描了它剩下的部分，并设法推断出这个机构里所有齿轮的情况。
cues.en: And people have uh run scans on on what is left of this and managed to deduce what all the gears were in this mechanism.

cues.zh: 这和我第一次听到这个消息时想的非常不一样。
cues.en: And it's very different from what I thought when I first heard news about this.

cues.zh: 我当时想，哦，希腊肯定有一些可爱的小齿轮装置。
cues.en: I thought like, oh, they must have had some cute little gear things in Greece.

cues.zh: 这很令人惊讶。
cues.en: That's surprising.

cues.zh: 不过让我给大家看看，这个装置公认复原图的规模有多大。
cues.en: Uh but let me just show you the scale of the generally agreed upon reconstruction of what this device actually was.

cues.zh: 这看起来齿轮很多，对吧？
cues.en: That seems like a lot of gears, right?

cues.zh: 但等等，还有更多。
cues.en: But wait, there's more.

cues.zh: 所以古希腊就有了这个。
cues.en: So ancient Greece had that.

cues.zh: 但那并不是我们今天对古希腊的印象，对吧？
cues.en: But that is not the picture that we have today of ancient Greece, right?

cues.zh: 要意识到的是，这些东西不是凭空出现的。不是某天还完全没有齿轮，第二天就有人造出了这个，对吧？
cues.en: And the thing to realize is you don't just get here from nothing. It's not like one day there weren't any gears and then the next day some guy makes this, right?

cues.zh: 你需要一整套科学发展的过程，才能创造出如此精密的东西。
cues.en: You need a whole process of science to create something that sophisticated.

cues.zh: 而今天我们对这些过程一无所知，对吧？
cues.en: And we don't know anything about that today, right?

cues.zh: 这一切都失传了。
cues.en: All of that was lost.

cues.zh: 我还可以不停地举例子。
cues.en: And I could go on and on with examples.

cues.zh: 历史上有很多类似的事情，但我们没时间展开。
cues.en: There's a whole bunch of things from history that are like this, but we don't have time.

cues.zh: 呃，我只想重申一下，我们现在生活在一个非常幸运的时代，技术已经长期处于良好状态。
cues.en: Uh I just want to restate that right now we live in a very privileged time uh where technology has been in a good shape for a long time.

cues.zh: 我们看到它在不断变好，于是就以为历史的自然进程就是技术总会进步，而这些历史时刻只是小插曲，或者只是我们听说过的事情。
cues.en: We see it getting better and so we imagine that the natural course of history is that technology always improves and that these moments in history are just like little blips or something that we heard about.

cues.zh: 但它们不只是小插曲。实际上，世界历史的常态就是：伟大的技术成就完全失传，因为创造这些成就的文明衰落了，或者，你知道，经历了一种软性衰落——没能把知识传承到未来，对吧？
cues.en: But they're not just little blips. It's actually sort of the regular course of world history that great achievements in technology just get completely lost because the civilizations that made those achievements fell or you know, had a sort of a soft fall where they failed to propagate the knowledge into the future, right?

cues.zh: 技术一直在倒退，不只是古代，现代也是如此，对吧？
cues.en: Technology goes backward all the time and not just in ancient history, also in the modern day, right?

cues.zh: 我们一直在丢失知识。
cues.en: We lose knowledge all the time.

cues.zh: 所以我要读一段对 Bob Colwell 的采访节选。他曾担任 Intel 的首席微处理器架构师一段时间，但这段采访是在那之前。
cues.en: So I'm going to read an excerpt from an interview with Bob Colwell, who was the chief microprocessor architect at Intel for a while, but this interview is from before that.

cues.zh: 这段采访来自硅谷蓬勃发展的年代，当时他在一家名为 Multiflow 的初创公司工作。
cues.en: It was from the booming days of Silicon Valley when he worked at a startup called Multiflow.

cues.zh: 他们当时在尝试做一款超长指令字处理器，那时这还是个新的实验性想法。
cues.en: They were trying to make a very large instruction word processor when that was a new experimental idea.

cues.zh: 嗯，而且他们遇到了很多问题，比如你设计芯片时用的是其他厂商的元件，而他就是没法让任何东西可靠工作。
cues.en: Um and they were having a lot of problems like when you try to design the chip, you're using components from other manufacturers and he just couldn't get anything to work reliably.

cues.zh: 他当时就想，搞什么鬼，对吧？
cues.en: And he was like, what what the hell, right?

cues.zh: 所以他说，嗯，我和 Rich Leth 一路朝圣般地去了得克萨斯州理查森的德州仪器，然后我们说，
cues.en: So he says, um Rich Leth and I made a pilgrimage down to Texas Instruments in Richardson, Texas and we said,

cues.zh: 据我们所能判断，你们的很多芯片都不能正常工作，这会让你们感到意外吗？
cues.en: as best as we can tell, many of your chips don't work properly and does this come as a surprise to you?

cues.zh: 我多少预料到他们会说，什么，你疯了吧，是你们搞错了吧。
cues.en: I half expected them to say, what, you're out of your mind, you've done something wrong.

cues.zh: 拜托，你们根本不懂自己在干什么，去用别人的芯片吧。
cues.en: Come on, you don't know what you're doing, go use somebody else's chips.

cues.zh: 但并没有，他们说，是啊，我们知道，让我看看你们的清单。
cues.en: But no, they said, yeah, we know, let me see your list.

cues.zh: 他们看了看清单，说：这里还有更多你不知道的问题。
cues.en: And they looked at the list and said, well, here's some more that you don't know about.

cues.zh: 顺便说一下，不只是 TI。
cues.en: And by the way, it wasn't just TI.

cues.zh: 他们的零件并不比别人的差。
cues.en: Their parts were no worse than anybody else's.

cues.zh: Motorola 的不行，Fairchild 的不行，他们都有这个问题。
cues.en: Motorola were no good, Fairchild were no good, they all had this problem.

cues.zh: 于是我问 TI：整个行业怎么会同时栽在同一个问题上？
cues.en: And so I asked TI, how did the entire industry fall on its face at the same time?

cues.zh: 我们拼了命地在你的硅片缺陷上做变通，把自己都快搞死了。
cues.en: We are killing ourselves trying to work around the shortcomings in your silicon.

cues.zh: 那家伙说，第一代晶体管逻辑是老一辈的白胡子工程师做的，他们真的懂自己在干什么。
cues.en: And the guy said, the first generation of transistor logic was done by the old graybeard guys who really knew what they were doing.

cues.zh: 新一代则是刚出校门的孩子做的，他们根本不知道要去问封装方式的改变会对感性尖峰造成什么影响，对吧？
cues.en: The new generation was done by kids who were straight out of school who didn't know to ask what the change in packaging would do to inductive spikes, right?

cues.zh: 所以当你在芯片上某些位置改变电压时，就会产生磁场，事情就是这样。
cues.en: So when you change the voltage in places on a chip, it generates a magnetic field because that's just what happens.

cues.zh: 当这些领域在芯片上相互作用时，糟糕，那就糟了，对吧？
cues.en: And when those fields interact across a chip, bad, it's bad, right?

cues.zh: 而且你知道，设计这些芯片的新人不知道要认真对待这一点。
cues.en: And the you know, the new people designing these chips didn't know uh to take that seriously.

cues.zh: 嗯，这就是技术退化的原因，或者至少是原因之一，对吧？
cues.en: Um and that's why technology degrades or it's at least one reason, right?

cues.zh: 代代相传需要大量精力和努力，嗯，这些重要的事情是你胜任工作所必须知道的
cues.en: It takes a lot of energy and effort to communicate from generation to generation, uh these important things that you need to know in order to do a competent job

cues.zh: 在制造技术的过程中，这种传播过程会有损失
cues.en: making the technology, and there are losses in that communication process

cues.zh: 几乎不可避免。
cues.en: almost inevitably.

cues.zh: 如果没有这种代际知识传承，文明可能会灭亡，因为那些文明所依赖的技术会退化并失效。
cues.en: And without this generational transfer of knowledge, civilizations can die because the technology that those civilizations depend on degrades and fails.

cues.zh: 那么让我们谈谈一个衰落的文明，实际上是一整组文明。
cues.en: So let's talk about a civilization that fell, actually a whole group of civilizations.

cues.zh: 呃，我接下来要展示的图表来自 YouTube 上一场讲座，叫《1177 BC：文明崩溃之年》，主讲是 Eric Klein。
cues.en: Uh the diagrams I'm going to show here are from a lecture you can find on YouTube called 1177 BC, the year civilization collapsed, by Eric Klein.

cues.zh: 嗯，我们讲的是青铜时代晚期，那时有不少文明，你们可能听说过一些，
cues.en: Um, and we're talking about the late Bronze Age, which was the time of a number of civilizations, you've heard of probably,

cues.zh: 比如埃及人、迈锡尼希腊人，或者赫梯人、巴比伦人。
cues.en: like the Egyptians or the Mycenaean Greeks, right, or the Hittites, the Babylonians.

cues.zh: 嗯，所以这个文明，或者说这个文明网络，大致横跨美索不达米亚和地中海。
cues.en: Um and uh so this civilization or this network of civilizations was sort of spanning Mesopotamia and the Mediterranean Sea.

cues.zh: 他们发展出了相当发达的贸易网络。
cues.en: And they had developed quite a uh sophisticated network of trade.

cues.zh: 在这张图里，每个点代表一个文明，连线则是这些文明之间已建立的通信和贸易路线。
cues.en: So in this graph here, each of these points is one of the civilizations and the lines are, you know, established communication and trade routes between those civilizations.

cues.zh: 虽然它们并非全都彼此相连，但互联程度足够高，使你可以相对高效地
cues.en: And whereas not all of them were connected to all of the other ones, they were interconnected enough that you could relatively efficiency efficiently

cues.zh: 在需要时把东西从一处运到另一处，这一点非常重要。
cues.en: route things from one place to another if you needed to, and that was very important.

cues.zh: 因为青铜——这个文明在防御等方面依赖它——
cues.en: Because bronze, which this civilization depended on for things like defense,

cues.zh: 呃，在当时很难制造。
cues.en: uh was hard to make back then.

cues.zh: 呃，你得把铜和锡结合起来才能造出来，而铜相对难找。
cues.en: Uh you had to do it by combining copper and tin, and copper was relatively hard to find.

cues.zh: 铜可以在塞浦路斯岛等地找到，而锡也非常难找。
cues.en: And was found in places like the island of Cyprus, and tin was also really hard to find.

cues.zh: 而锡则是在离那些铜产地很远的地方找到的，
cues.en: And was found very far away from those copper places,

cues.zh: 比如在阿富汗，而你总得设法持续把这些东西运来运去
cues.en: like in Afghanistan, and you you somehow had to persistently ship these things around

cues.zh: 才能造出青铜，以及你的社会所依赖的其他东西。
cues.en: in order to make your bronze and the other things that your society depended on.

cues.zh: 没人确切知道这场崩溃中到底发生了什么。
cues.en: And nobody's sure exactly what happened in this collapse.

cues.zh: 但人们认为，是某种环境压力因素引发了它，比如曾发生过大旱，也有人推测可能还有洪水。
cues.en: But people believe there was some kind of environmental stressor to kick it off, like there was a huge drought, possibly also some floods are theorized.

cues.zh: 这导致一些人开始攻击另一些人。
cues.en: And this led to some people attacking some other people.

cues.zh: 于是，你可能得开始把船用于防御，而不是贸易。
cues.en: And, you know, maybe you need to start using your ships for defense instead of trading.

cues.zh: 基本上就是，从所有这些繁荣的文明，到100年后，它们一个都不剩了。
cues.en: And uh basically you went from all these flourishing civilizations to 100 years later, none of them were left.

cues.zh: 我说一个都不剩，甚至不是指那些国家消失了。
cues.en: And by none of them were left, I don't even mean that like, the nation states were gone.

cues.zh: 而是许多城市被烧成了平地。
cues.en: Like many of the cities were burned to the ground.

cues.zh: 嗯，语言和文化也没能存续下来。
cues.en: Um, and the languages and cultures don't survive.

cues.zh: 尽管他们是通过在石头上压刻来书写，但就是没人能翻译那些语言。
cues.en: Even though they wrote by, you know, pressing things into stone, like nobody was able to translate those languages.

cues.zh: 即使在今天，我们仍然无法翻译其中很多内容。
cues.en: Even today, we still can't translate a lot of them.

cues.zh: 所以，很多知识就在这里失传了。
cues.en: So like so much knowledge was lost here.

cues.zh: 嗯，在这次崩塌中，呃，我们之后会再回到这一点。
cues.en: Um, in this collapse, uh we'll we'll get back to it later.

cues.zh: 但我想以某种方式把它和现代联系起来，而我接下来演讲的论点是：软件实际上正在衰退。
cues.en: But so I want to bridge this to the modern day in some way and my thesis for the rest of this talk is that software is actually in decline right now.

cues.zh: 呃，这也许是一种软性衰退，只是让事情对我们很不方便，但之后可能导致硬性衰退。
cues.en: Uh it's in maybe a soft decline that just makes things really inconvenient for us, but it could lead to a hard decline later on.

cues.zh: 因为我们的文明依赖软件。我们把它放到所有地方，我们所有的通信系统都是软件，我们的交通工具也是软件。
cues.en: Because our civilization depends on software. We put it everywhere, all our communication systems are software, our vehicles are software.

cues.zh: 所以，你知道，我们现在有飞机会因为糟糕的软件、而且仅仅因为糟糕的软件，导致数百人死亡，对吧？
cues.en: So, you know, we now have airplanes that kill hundreds of people due to bad software and bad software only, right?

cues.zh: 那些飞机没有其他问题。
cues.en: There was no other problem with those airplanes.

cues.zh: 呃，
cues.en: Um,

cues.zh: 现在，如果我说软件正在衰落，我觉得大多数人不会相信我。
cues.en: Now, I don't think most people would believe me if I say software is in decline.

cues.zh: 它看起来确实一片繁荣。
cues.en: It sure seems like it's flourishing.

cues.zh: 所以我至少得说服你，这是一个合理的观点，而这就是我接下来演讲的目标。
cues.en: So I have to convince you at least that this is a plausible perspective and that's my goal for the rest of this talk.

cues.zh: 对此我要说的是，这些崩溃，就像我们正在谈的，
cues.en: And what I'll say about that is these collapses, like we're talking about,

cues.zh: 那场青铜时代崩溃规模巨大，所有这些文明都被摧毁了，但它花了100年。
cues.en: that Bronze Age collapse was massive, like all these civilizations were destroyed, but it took a 100 years.

cues.zh: 所以如果你处在那场崩溃的开端，也就是头20年，你可能会想，嗯，情况不如20年前好，
cues.en: So if you were at the beginning of that collapse in the first 20 years, you might think, well, things aren't as good as they were 20 years ago,

cues.zh: 但没关系，我们基本还是老样子，对吧？
cues.en: but it's fine, we're basically the same, right?

cues.zh: 但接着你会一直这么想，一直这么想。每过20年，又有几座城市被烧成废墟，然后最终
cues.en: But then you keep thinking that, you keep thinking that. Every 20 years another couple of cities get burned to the ground and then eventually

cues.zh: 就几乎什么都不剩了，对吧？
cues.en: there's like nothing, right?

cues.zh: 呃，罗马帝国的衰亡大约持续了300年。
cues.en: Um, fall of the Roman Empire was about 300 years.

cues.zh: 所以，如果你正处在一场如此缓慢的崩溃之中，你会意识到吗？你会知道它在内部看起来是什么样吗？
cues.en: So if you're in the middle of a very slow collapse like that, would you recognize it? Would you know what it looked like from the inside?

cues.zh: 所以，当然，我预计别人对我这番话的回应会是：你疯了，软件业明明发展得很好。
cues.en: So, of course, I expect the reply to what I'm saying to be, you're crazy, software is doing great.

cues.zh: 看看所有这些互联网公司，赚着大把的钱，改变着我们的生活方式，你知道，我会说，是的，这一切都在发生。
cues.en: Look at all these internet companies that are making all this money and changing the way that we live, you know, and I would say, yes, that is all happening.

cues.zh: 呃，但真正发生的是，软件一直在搭硬件的便车。
cues.en: Uh, but what is really happening is that software has been free riding on hardware.

cues.zh: 过去几十年里，硬件技术取得了惊人的进步。
cues.en: For the past many decades, we've had amazing advances in hardware technology.

cues.zh: 计算机越来越快。
cues.en: Computers keep getting faster and faster.

cues.zh: 呃，我们竟然做到了这一点，这真的是人类历史上最伟大的成就之一。
cues.en: Um, it's really one of the greatest accomplishments in human history that we've somehow managed to do that.

cues.zh: 软件变好了——加引号的“变好”，呃，是因为有了更好的硬件来运行它。
cues.en: And software gets better in air quotes, uh because it has better hardware to run on.

cues.zh: 这是主要原因。
cues.en: That's the main reason.

cues.zh: 软件技术本身已经很久没有真正的进步了。
cues.en: Software technology itself has not improved in quite a while.

cues.zh: 我这么说，对吧？
cues.en: I claim, right?

cues.zh: 你可能会说，可你看过去几年我们做出了这么多很酷的东西。
cues.en: And you can say, but look at all these examples of cool stuff we can do, even in the past couple of years.

cues.zh: 比如 AlphaGo 是一个能在围棋上击败人类玩家的 AI。
cues.en: So like AlphaGo was an AI that'll beat human players at Go.

cues.zh: 或者你打开 Instagram 之类的应用，就能把自己的脸换成别人的脸。
cues.en: And you can go on like Instagram or whatever app and like make your face look like somebody else's face.

cues.zh: 太疯狂了。以前我们做不到这个。
cues.en: That's crazy. We didn't used to be able to do that.

cues.zh: 这没错。
cues.en: And that's true.

cues.zh: 但第一，呃，这些大多 again 都是硬件变快带来的产物。
cues.en: But one, uh most of these again are products of hardware being fast.

cues.zh: 我们现在做的这些酷东西，大多都归功于机器学习算法，而且你知道，它们目前确实依赖大量的计算
cues.en: Most of these cool things that we do now are due to machine learning algorithms and it's you know, those really are relying on quantity of computation right now

cues.zh: 才能产生令人印象深刻的结果。
cues.en: to produce impressive results.

cues.zh: 很难想象 20 年前用我们当时的电脑就能训练出 AlphaGo，对吧？
cues.en: It's hard to imagine being able to train AlphaGo 20 years ago on the computers we had at that time, right?

cues.zh: 所以这并不是说……这里确实有软件技术的进步，对吧？
cues.en: So it's not a There are software technology improvements here, right?

cues.zh: 机器学习的算法确实变得更好了。
cues.en: Machine learning learning algorithms have legitimately gotten better.

cues.zh: 但关于这一点有两点要说。嗯，
cues.en: But there's two things to say about that. Um,

cues.zh: 嗯，关于这一点，我要说的重点是：这只是实际软件技术中的一小部分，对吧？
cues.en: Uh well the the main thing to say about it, I will say is just that it's a minority of actual software technology, right?

cues.zh: 所以在我们运行的这么多东西里，真正运行机器学习算法并产生实际惊艳结果的那部分
cues.en: So the of the volume of things that we run, the thing that runs the machine learning algorithm that produces the actual impressive result

cues.zh: 只是程序里非常小的一部分。
cues.en: is a very small piece of the program.

cues.zh: 其实一旦你理解了数学，它就非常简单。
cues.en: It's actually really simple uh once you understand the math.

cues.zh: 尤其是如果你不需要训练它，只需要使用它，对吧？
cues.en: And especially if you don't have to train it, if you just have to use it, right?

cues.zh: 比如你手机上有个 App，能对你的照片做点有趣的处理，其中真正让我们觉得酷、真正有价值的那部分功能，
cues.en: Um and so when you take an app on your phone like that that does something funny with your picture, the part of it that does the thing that we think is cool and really value,

cues.zh: 那段软件跟你加载人脸位图、响应用户输入事件之类的所有东西比起来，简直简单得不得了，对吧？
cues.en: that piece of software is tremendously simple compared to all the stuff about like loading the bitmap for your face or responding to user input events, right?

cues.zh: 而那部分软件体量巨大、极其复杂，恰恰是正在崩坏的部分。
cues.en: That part of the software is huge and complicated and is the part that's kind of falling apart.

cues.zh: 所以我会说，软件领域有的是局部的小技术进步，比如机器学习，
cues.en: So I would characterize software as having small local technological improvements like machine learning,

cues.zh: 但整个领域的其余部分，整体上是停滞甚至退化的。
cues.en: um, with overall inertia or degradation in the rest of the field.

cues.zh: 可我们还是对这些进步印象深刻，对吧？
cues.en: And we're very impressed by the improvements though, right?

cues.zh: 接下来我尽量说明一下那些退化的部分。
cues.en: And let me illustrate the degradation parts uh as best I can.

cues.zh: 也就是说，我们已经根本不指望软件能正常工作了。
cues.en: And it's to say that we simply don't expect software to work anymore.

cues.zh: 我不确定这是从什么时候开始的。
cues.en: And I'm not sure when this happened.

cues.zh: 你知道，计算机一直有点“怪”的名声，
cues.en: You know, computers always had a reputation for being a little bit funny,

cues.zh: 呃，但你知道，如果回到几十年前，
cues.en: uh but it you know, if you go back many decades ago,

cues.zh: 那通常是因为它们不够用户友好，或者……
cues.en: it was generally due to like not being user friendly or or

cues.zh: 很难弄明白怎么用。
cues.en: hard to understand how to use it.

cues.zh: 呃，但今天，如果你用某个程序，它出了点错，你只会想：是啊，这是软件嘛，
cues.en: Um but today, if you're using a program and it does something wrong, you're just like, yeah, it's software,

cues.zh: 重启一下，随便吧。
cues.en: restart it, whatever.

cues.zh: 以前可不是这样。
cues.en: And that didn't used to be.

cues.zh: 如果我们的标准随着时间不断下降，那还能降到多低才会变得不可持续？
cues.en: And if our standards are shrinking over time, how low can they shrink before it becomes unsustainable?

cues.zh: 所以我决定，呃，这么说：
